newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse meat firms seen growing - brokerage.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse meat firms seen growing - brokerage.

text.p: Five meat processing companies listed on the Warsaw bourse are likely to increase their market share, benefitting from holding structures and the weakening of other firms in the sector, a brokerage said.
Farm Food, Pekpol, Sokolow, Drosed and Indykpol, considered the strongest in the sector, now hold 8.5 percent of the market.

"Consolidation of the sector around strong meat-processing firms will continue and give those firms a larger domestic market share," Andrzej Kosinski, an analyst at Kredyt Bank brokerage told a seminar on the meat-processing sector.
Sokolow said it wanted to gain 15 percent of the domestic market in the next three years and Farm Food said it sought to have up to 15 percent by 2000.
Farm Food already has a 72.3 percent stake in Zaklady Miesne Jaroslaw SA, Sokolow has 45 percent in Zaklady Miesne Kolo SA and both said they were looking for more aquisitions.
Pekpol has eight subsidaries, while Drosed bought Pomorskie Zaklady Drobiarskie Janicki in Torun earlier in the year.
Kosinski said the meat firms listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange would also be benefitting from possible bankruptcies of smaller meat companies.
Polish meat firms employing over 50 people recorded a net loss of 85 million zlotys last year, while the five listed on the bourse had a 28 million zloty net profit.
The brokerage expected annual meat consumption to rise to 71.8 kg per person by 2000 and to 80.3 kg in 2005 from 64.6 kg in 1995.
